c.h:
Summoning training can become very expensive and tedious, but familiars at higher levels make Summoning a rewarding skill.

Free-to-play players can gain experience up to level 5 and continue to collect gold charms after level 5, which may be useful if you intend on becoming members eventually.

To begin training the Summoning skill, players may complete Wolf Whistle, which will grant 276 experience to Summoning (increasing the player's level to 4), as well as 275 gold charms (enough for level 16, or 5 on F2P). After that you will have to collect your own charms.

Free-to-play players can collect additional gold charms from collecting one free sample from Pikkupstix's Summoning Shop or by killing troll brutes and troll chuckers in Burthorpe. Then create dreadfowl pouch to train the Summoning skill to level 5.

The Shaman's outfit can be obtained by crafting pouches at the Shrine of Inanna, with 3,600 pouches required for the full shaman's outfit.

The only viable way of training Summoning is to create Summoning pouches. To begin making a Summoning pouch, the following are required:

  • An empty pouch, which can be bought from Pikkupstix for 1 gp each. (Not required for Summoning within Daemonheim)
  • A quantity of charms, which must be collected by the player through monster killing and other methods. Good ways to do this are listed below.
  • A large number of spirit shards, which can be bought from Pikkupstix for 25 coins each or you can buy a set of 5,000 for 125,000. (Not required for Summoning within Daemonheim), spirit shards can also be bought at the Grand Exchange. Though the guide price is not always 25 coins (currently 24 coins), it is rare that anyone will sell it for anything less than that. On the other hand, spirit shards can be sold by pet store owners (such as the one in Taverley) in arbitrarily large amounts, so spirit shards are essentially equivalent to 25 coins. Finally, spirit shards are one of the drops from opening geodes, gathered by mining.
  • A tertiary ingredient which is specific to the creature you are creating, similar to the secondary ingredients used in Herblore.

If you have access to Prifddinas use the attuned crystal teleport seed and teleport to Amlodd district, followed by a short run to the Summoning obelisk, then teleport to Ithell district to re-supply with bank preset and Beasts of Burden (BoB) set-up. Exchange pouches for shards with Lord Amlodd if you feel like it. Note that doing this when Voice of Seren is active in Amlodd district results in more shards returned, and more XP.

With the use of Bogrog or Lord Amlodd the pouches you make can be turned back into shards; the number of shards returned to you is 70% of the pouch cost. With this in mind, you can drastically reduce the number of shards you have to originally buy by continually converting the pouches you make back into shards. Players with the hard Tirannwn achievements completed should use Lord Amlodd for all shard returns as he will instead return 77% of the pouch cost, further reducing the number of shards needed for training.

c.t: How many spirit shards do I buy?
c.g: How many spirit shards do I buy?
c.h:
Since spirit shards can be sold back for the same price they were purchased at either a Summoning shop or the Taverley pet shop owner (who will buy shards in quantities larger than 500), it is simpler to take an educated guess at how many shards you'll need, and sell back any extras.

With the use of Bogrog in Gu'Tanoth or Lord Amlodd in Prifddinas, you can turn the pouches you make back into spirit shards; the amount of shards you get is usually 70% (77% with Lord Amlodd with the hard Tirannwn achievements completed) of the required shard number for the pouch. Utilising this, the number of shards you need to initially buy can be drastically reduced, however the effectiveness of this varies greatly with number of shards you initially have and the number of times you are willing to exchange your pouches. Also, some pouches may be worth more if sold rather than converted. See Calculators/Shard swap.

The formula which calculates the effective number of shards owned is as follows: \sum_{i=0}^{n}S\times{x}^{\ i} = S \times \frac{1}{1-x} \left(1 - x^{n+1}\right)

where,

  • S is initial amount of shards
  • n is number of shard return iterations
  • x is 0.7 if using Bogrog or Amlodd, 0.77 if using Amlodd with the hard Tirannwn achievements.
  • i is summation parameter

The calculator below can be used for this summation for any integer S,0 \leq S \leq 2\,147\,483\,647 and any integer n, 1 \leq n \leq 100: template = Calculator:Summoning shard return form = CalcForm result = CalcResult param = shards|Initial shards|1|int param = returns|Number of returns|0|int param = location|Location|Bogrog/Amlodd|select|Bogrog/Amlodd,Amlodd (with Hard Tirannwn achievements)||Amlodd with the Hard tirannwn achievements returns 77% of the shard cost instead of 70%.

Calculator requires JavaScript

Please submit the form to display the results.

However, it becomes tedious to recalculate this continuously to find the required number of shards you need initially. It is much easier to first decide how many times you are willing to do spend the time returning your pouches into shards. This will dictate what percentage increase you will ultimately get (regardless of initial count). Amlodd is strongly recommended if available due to how close it is to a teleport and bank chest, as well as being next to an obelisk for creating pouches. The increases can be seen below:

The maximum possible number to divide by is 3 and a third (3.33). As shown in the table, to get close to this number requires many trips.

For example, let's say you needed 55,000 shards to attain a certain level, the first thing you do need to decide upon is how many times you would be willing to visit a location you can exchange pouches for shards. In this example, let's use Bogrog, and say you are willing to do this 10 times (any more than this, the gain in shards is minimal; for example doing 20 trips instead of 10 when having an initial starting shard count of 100,000 only yields an extra 6,405 shards). The amount of trips you are willing to do is something you have to decide.

At 10 trips, the increase is 227% so the effective amount will be 327% of the initial amount, or 3.27 times the initial amount. You then divide 55,000 by 3.27 to get 16,820 (rounded up). Therefore, to effectively have 55,000 shards whilst willing to do 10 trips to Bogrog you only initially need to have 16,820 spirit shards. In practice, however, you may need extra shards, as after some shard return trades, you may end up with so few shards it won't even be enough to make one pouch.
c.a: How many spirit shards do I buy?

c.h:
When making pouches, you should have the charms you are using, empty pouches, spirit shards, and the rest of the inventory filled with the tertiary ingredient.

  • It is highly recommended to use bank presets to load the required setup, so you can instantly load the required items into your inventory on each bank trip.
  • Note that the charms, pouch, and shards are placed at the end of the inventory to facilitate training with familiars using the drop trick.
  • Because these methods require a lot of running, you may want to have infinite run energy, equip weight reducing equipment, or use a spirit terrorbird for infinite run (not recommended as a beast of burden for the tertiary ingredients can get you better xp rates).
    • You can also drink energy potions or super energy potions from time to time to refill your run energy.

The simplest method consists of running between a bank and an obelisk. The obelisks closest to a bank are:

  1. Menaphos Merchant district in Menaphos
  2. Amlodd district in Prifddinas
  3. Taverley

The Taverley and Prifddinas bank locations are near a house portal, so you could set your house to be in Taverley or Prifddinas and use a house teleport to shorten your trips. Alternatively, an Attuned crystal teleport seed is good for navigating within Prifddinas.

There is a specific order of actions needed when using Beasts of burden to make pouches. To set up, the stack of pouches, charms, and shards should be the last three items in the inventory. This method does not work if they are the first three items. In addition, for maximum efficiency, the tertiary ingredient of the pouch should:

  • Be able to be carried by the BOB. (e.g. light cores for light creatures would not work)
  • Have the action on the ability bar to be "drop". (e.g. water talismans for geyser titans would not work as the action is "locate" instead of "drop")

Here is the procedure for each trip.

  1. Fill inventory and BOB's inventory with the tertiary ingredients and summoning supplies (using bank preset). Make sure to fill your BOB up to full, regardless of how many pouches you will be making.
  2. Get to the obelisk.
  3. Drop all tertiary items from inventory. Dropping should be performed with the action bar. Beware that some tertiary ingredients do not have "Drop" as their default option on the action bar. For such items, one can drop them by moving the action bar near the bottom of the client (but not snapped to the bottom) so that dropping can be achieved by alternating left and right clicks without moving the mouse.
  4. Retrieve all items from the BOB by clicking the retrieve button on the BOB interface. (This can be done through action bar.)
  5. Click the obelisk to make the first batch of pouches.
  6. Deposit all items to the BOB by clicking the deposit button on the interface. (This takes a single click, again, doable with action bar. This requires charms, shards, and pouches to be at the last three spots in the inventory. As you only retrieved 25 tertiary ingredients from the BOB, there should only be enough space to deposit all the pouches you just made, leaving the charms, shards, and pouches in your inventory)
  7. Pick up all of the dropped tertiary ingredients. This should be performed using Area loot so that picking up only takes one click and one keystroke.
  8. Make the second batch of pouches. It is totally normal to have some tertiary ingredients unused left in the BOB. Any ingredient after the 25th will not be used, but are essential to be there for this method to work.
  9. Restock, possibly using a bank teleport.

Above level 57 Summoning, you can use a spirit kyatt to teleport near the Piscatoris summoning obelisk, and use War's Retreat Teleport, a Tokkul-Zo, ring of duelling, or grace of the elves with the first portal at the Max Guild garden set to Deep Sea Fishing hub to bank. Using this method it is possible to make over 2700 pouches per hour, making it one of the fastest ways to train Summoning.

Below level 57 Summoning, you can use Phoenix Lair Teleports and run north-east to the Piscatoris obelisk.

Should the player not wish to spend money on spirit kyatt pouches, they can use the nature grotto in Mort Myre Swamp. This method requires a Tokkul-Zo, access to the fairy ring network, and the Mort Myre shortcut unlocked from Temple Trekking (total follower level 100). Start at the TzHaar Fight Cave bank, and use the fairy ring to Canifis (code ). Run south to gate and right-click the option 'Quick travel' for shortcut to the Nature Grotto. Make the pouches in the grotto, and bank using the Tokkul-Zo. This method is slower than using a spirit kyatt, but faster than running to Pikkupstix's house in Taverley.

It is also possible to use the balloon transport system to make pouches in Taverley. Equip a ring of duelling and have charges stored with the balloon assistants, take a balloon to Taverley, make pouches, then teleport to the bank at Castle Wars.

If the player has access to Prifddinas (requires completion of Plague's End) they can use Crystal teleport seeds to rapidly teleport to the Amlodd Clan district to craft pouches and then back to either the Ithell Clan or the Trahaearn Clan district to bank. This is made even more efficient if the player has the 85 Smithing required to craft an Attuned crystal teleport seed which has infinite charges and thus doesn't need to be changed out every few trips. If the player is training in Prifddinas, it is recommended to wait until the Voice of Seren is affecting the Amlodd district in order to take advantage of the 20% base experience buff it provides.

Using a portable fairy ring with the coordinates to travel to the Amlodd district obelisk appears to be the fastest way to get to an obelisk for making pouches.

The Shrine of Inanna is a free-to-play area located on Havenhythe near the village of Wendlewick which contains three summoning obelisks. Rather than instantly infusing all pouches in your inventory in one go, pouches are slowly infused one-by-one at these obelisks. At any given time, one of the three obelisks will be empowered; infusing pouches at the empowered obelisk grants a stacking Spirit Plane Connection buff which increased experience per pouch made, and gives a scaling chance to infuse pouches without using any ingredients. As long as this buff is maintained above 90%, training summoning here is beneficial for maximizing experience gained from a charm supply whilst minimizing costs from spirit shards and/or secondary ingredients.

Stacks are obtained at the same rate regardless of the type of pouch made. Therefore, if training with valuable charms or secondary ingredients, it is recommended to infuse cheaper pouches to build up Spirit Plane Connection to 100% before infusing more costly pouches.

A bank is located to the west by the tree farm which is unlocked by completing the Trader Woes achievement. Alternatively, a fairy ring is located to the southeast of the shrine accessed through the code . This allows for faster banking by teleporting to a bank (such as War's Retreat Teleport or Prifddinas lodestone), then teleporting to the player owned house using House Teleport and then using a fairy ring furniture to return quickly. Optionally, one can bring a Beast of Burden familiar to carry extra secondary ingredients and extend the number of pouches made per trip. However, ingredients and pouches must be manually exchanged between the inventories of the player and familiar by dragging items between slots as the pouches are infused, requiring significantly more effort.

The Shrine awards 1 Blessings of the Wolf per pouch created, which can be used to purchase the Shaman's outfit at the Shrine of the Spirit Wolves shop (3,600 for the full set plus the headress add-on).

Occasionally, a Spirit Wolf will spawn in the centre of the three obelisks that will take an offering of 100 spirit shards to empower the player with Spirit Communion. For the next 100 pouches made at any of the three obelisks, Spirit Plane Connection will not decrease and pouch creation time is reduced by 0.6 seconds. Spirit Communion will persist even after leaving the shrine, and has the additional benefit of preventing Spirit Plane Connection stacks from depleting over time while the player is away. For this reason, it is recommended to obtain the Spirit Communion buff before ending a training session so Spirit Plane Connection stacks won't need to be built up again when returning later.

c.a: Maximising xp/charm, reasonable cost per pouch

c.h:
The most efficient way to train the Summoning skill from max level to 200m XP is to use magic notepaper or a portable deposit box placed next to the Taverley summoning obelisk and make geyser titan pouches. If these options are unavailable, a secondary and tertiary method have been provided below.

  • The setup below yields a base XP rate of approximately 11.7m/hr for the most efficient method. The secondary method and tertiary method yield base XP rates of approximately 4.62m/hr and 3.72m/hr respectively.
  • These rates do not include any items associated with Treasure Hunter such as advanced pulse cores and cinder cores, or global boosts such as Bonus XP, the clan avatar buff and the sceptre of enchantment buff. The boost from a Summoning focus to XP is not factored in due to the high GP/XP. Including these buffs, a user can earn a Summoning XP rate using the primary method in excess of 26.8m/hr not accounting for DXP.
  • If not all items are owned, use the next best available item, however the XP rates will need to be recalculated by the user.

c.t: Basic preset for training to 200m XP
c.h:
Equipment
  • Shaman's outfit for experience boost, modified headgear will additionally save charms
  • Summoning cape to save charms
  • Any augmented main-hand with Wise 4 and Mobile, Wilderness sword 4 is universally good as this option
    • Any off-hand weapon to use Bladed Dive if necessary, but regular Dive is better as you always target the floor instead of accidentally targeting NPCs or scenery
  • Spirit onyx or any spirit gem owned, leave empty if none are owned - equip attuned crystal teleport seed if no spirit gems owned and using Amlodd
  • Grasping rune pouch with runes to use Taverley Teleport, or 3 air runes, 1 fire rune, and 1 law in inventory to use once and keep open inventory space
  • Grace of the elves for 0 step bank, optional
Inventory setup
  • Torstol incense sticks - apply at bank and exclude from preset to save inventory space
Relics and boosts
  • Inspire Awe
  • Summoning focus not recommended due to GP/XP but wealthier players may consider it worthwhile.
c.a: Basic preset for training to 200m XP

c.h:
Primary method (Taverley buy/sell)=

How it works:
  1. Deploy a portable deposit box, or find an existing one someone else has deployed. Players can use magic notepaper on created pouch if a portable deposit box is not available.
  2. Withdraw the pouches, shards, charms and 500 of the tertiary item (noted) in your inventory (you can load a bank preset)
  3. Head to the Taverley obelisk and sell the noted tertiary items to the shopkeeper Magestix
  4. Now the backpack has space, buy back the tertiary items from Magestix to get it un-noted (costs only a few coins)
  5. Click on the obelisk to create the pouches
  6. Deposit your pouches into the portable deposit box (be careful not to dump your entire inventory) or note them with magic notepaper
  7. Repeat from step 4 till you run out of tertiaries, at which point repeat from step 2
  8. Your tertiary items will start to despawn if left in the shop for too long. Do not sell too many to the shopkeeper in a go.

This method can yield upwards of 15,000 pouches per hour. |-| Secondary method (Amlodd runs)=

How it works:
  1. Use an attuned crystal teleport seed to teleport to the Ithell district in Prifddinas
  2. Use this bank to withdraw your preset
  3. Travel north towards the Amlodd summoning obelisk (Dive west towards the robust glass machine, surge north, then surge north again across the bridge)
  4. Make your pouches on the obelisk
  5. Teleport back to the Ithell district using the teleport seed
  6. Repeat steps 2 to 5

This method can yield upwards of 5,900 pouches per hour. |-| Tertiary method (Attuned crystal seed method)=

This method should only be used if Double Surge and/or Dive is not owned, as this method is slower than teleporting back to Ithell.

How it works:
  1. Use an attuned crystal teleport seed to teleport to the Ithell district in Prifddinas
  2. Use this bank to withdraw your preset
  3. Use the Attuned crystal teleport seed again to teleport to the Amlodd district.
  4. Run west to the second square of the exposed tile on the ground and Bladed Dive directly in front of the obelisk
  5. Make your pouches on the obelisk
  6. Repeat steps 2 to 5

This method can yield upwards of 4,750 pouches per hour. |-|

This subsection presents a counterpoint to the previous section and argues that one should not always make the pouch that maximises experience per charm. Instead, Sacrificing a somewhat small amount of experience per charm in favour of slightly higher cost-effectiveness can imply an unexpectedly large savings of coins per experience point. This is a rather subtle consideration and has its share of limitations, as does the perspective in the previous subsection. Again, we ignore pouches that use untradeable ingredients for simplicity, but in practice, these pouches can make a difference in training.

Similar pouches using blue charms

Since the release of the Arch-Glacor, water talisman prices have crashed and therefore a player would prefer making Geyser titan pouches vs the next best alternative (rune minotaur).

Similar pouches using crimson charms

For crimson charms, Pack mammoths are the clear best pouch to make, but they require 99 Summoning and may be hard to trade. Further calculations show that pack yaks are usually the clear second-best pouch to make, but they require level 96 Summoning. Further calculations show that the next-best pouches to make (from the perspective in this section) are the Brawler/Deacon demons, then Granite lobsters, then Smoke devils, then Bloated leeches and finally pyrelords. Other pouches may give more experience but are far outclassed by the next-highest pouch in the aforementioned list from the point of view of relative opportunity cost.

Similar pouches using green charms

For green charms, one may find that Fruit bat pouches are actually preferable to Unicorn stallion pouches. This is because the implied cost per experience of preferring Unicorn stallion pouches over Fruit bat pouches must be (2641-813-24 - ( 2416-224-24 ) ) / (154.4 - 121.2) round 2 gp per experience point.

Similar pouches using gold charms

For gold charms, if one uses them at all, one may find that Spirit terrorbirds are actually preferable to Barker toads. This is because the implied cost per experience of preferring Barker toads over Spirit terrorbirds must be (1135-942-24 - ( 956-946-24 ) )/ (87.0 - 68.4) gp per experience point.

Further calculations

This article has omitted further comparisons such as Fire titans versus rune minotaurs, etc. One will find that the implied cost to prefer Rune minotaurs over Fire titans is very large. This analysis easily extends to using Summoning focuses. Assuming that one uses Summoning focuses for two comparable pouches, the cost of using the focus is the same for each option, so its cost can be cancelled out as before. The only difference is that now, both options have their experience reward multiplied by 1.2, so the implied relative tradeoff is multiplied by exactly 5/6 or about 0.833.

Further limitations
  • These calculations are somewhat sensitive to small price changes. For example, a drop in the price of Water talismans by 2000 coins, or about 40 percent, changes the implied relative tradeoff rate to (4285 + 2000 -549-24 - (3800-255-24) ) / 88 round 2 gp, and perhaps many players would accept this new tradeoff.
  • This method cannot be used to compare pouches used made with different charms.
  • This method also does not apply to pouches with a single untradeable component.
  • This method cannot compare pouches that use two tertiary ingredients (such as wolpertingers) with pouches which use only one tertiary ingredient (such as Swamp titans).
  • Often, when comparing two (comparable) pouches in this way, the higher-level pouch will be preferable because it might, for example, imply a relative cost of 5 coins per experience point, or maybe even a "negative cost" per point. Of course, this does not mean that one should always prefer to make the higher-level pouch because if ones current Summoning level is in between the two required levels, then one does not have any choice. However, this may serve as a strong incentive to reach the higher level without using any of that charm.

Example: best pouches if one accepts an implied relative tradeoff of 20 coins per experience point

The claims in this section are sensitive to price changes, so they can be out of date. This section does consider summoning focuses. Their use can significantly change the following lists.

For gold charms, the only acceptable pouches are the dreadfowl, spirit spider, and spirit terrorbird. All other pouches are unacceptable because the next-highest pouch in the aforementioned list yields an implied relative tradeoff of over 20 coins per experience point (and far more than 20 coins in some cases).

For green charms, the only acceptable pouches are the desert wyrm, compost mound, beaver, macaw, ibis (bunyip are barely worse than Ibises, subject to price changes), and Fruit bat. All other pouches are unacceptable. The fruit bat is far superior to the bunyip and only requires one higher level.

For crimson charms, the only acceptable pouches are the spirit scorpion, vampyre bat (barely not honey badger), pyrelord, bloated leech, smoke devil, granite lobster, the cheaper of brawler/deacon demon (barely not spirit dagannoth), wolpertinger, pack yak, and pack mammoth.

For blue charms, the only acceptable pouches are the albino rat, bronze minotaur, iron minotaur, spirit jelly (barely not steel minotaur), karamthulhu overlord, mithril minotaur, adamant minotaur, rune Minotaur, and fire titan.

Using Double Surge, Bladed Dive or Dive, and one teleport to bank

  • Prifddinas unlocked from completing Plague's End.
  • Bladed Dive or Dive and Double Surge unlocked from the Double Surge codex.
  • Attuned crystal teleport seed (level 85 Smithing required).
  • Mobile perk on a piece of augmented equipment or Shadow's Grace relic power activated.
  • 2 melee weapons for Bladed Dive or any melee weapon with laceration boots. No weapons needed if using Dive.

For greater efficiency, place the attuned crystal teleport seed on your action bar to activate it quicker.

After the following requirements have been met, the player can reach Amlodd's obelisk from Ithell in a matter of seconds. The runs are done in this order:

  1. Starting from the Ithell teleport's bank chest, withdraw (preferably from a bank preset) summoning-related items into the inventory.
  2. Use the first surge on the straightaway north.
  3. Use the second surge on the straightaway west.
  4. Use the Bladed Dive or Dive on the straightaway north to the obelisk. Be careful not to select an elf or the obelisk itself.
  5. Click on the obelisk and infuse pouch on obelisk.
  6. Activate the Attuned crystal teleport seed by clicking on it or using the action bar and teleport to Ithell (option 8) to bank.

Doing the following allows the player to make 15-18 second obelisk runs, depending on ping, human error, etc. The mobile perk or Shadow's Grace relic is necessary for the runs, as the cooldown for Surge is 20.4 seconds, which would ultimately slow the average run time.

It is also possible to exit the Ithell teleport location through the west instead of the north, past the harps and clay/sandstone rocks. However, there are different pathing obstacles here and includes having to Bladed Dive or Dive diagonally, so there is more room for error. Starting from the bank chest area, walk out west into the open, Bladed Dive or Dive diagonally towards the Robust glass machine, then line yourself up to Surge through the two arches up to the obelisk. Attempting to surge diagonally may sometimes surge you into the wrong direction, so try to leave the diagonal movement to Bladed Dive or Dive.

Either method drains run energy faster than can be naturally regenerated, so light-reducing gear or stamina regeneration methods should be utilised.

Secondary method using Bladed Dive or Dive and two teleports:

  • Prifddinas unlocked from completing Plague's End.
  • Attuned crystal teleport seed (level 85 Smithing required).
  • War's Retreat Teleport for fast banking without having to menu through the teleport seed.
  • Mobile perk on a piece of augmented equipment or Shadow's Grace relic activated.

For greater efficiency, place the attuned crystal teleport seed on your action bar to activate it quicker.

After the following requirements have been met, the player can reach Amlodd's obelisk from Ithell in a matter of seconds. The runs are done in this order:

  1. Starting from War's Retreat's bank chest, withdraw (preferably from a bank preset) summoning-related items into the inventory.
  2. Activate the Attuned crystal teleport seed by clicking on it or using the action bar and teleport to Amlodd (option 3).
  3. Run west to the second square of the exposed tile on the ground.
  4. Select Bladed Dive or Dive and click directly in front of the obelisk. Be careful not to select an elf or the obelisk itself.
  5. Click on the obelisk and infuse pouch on obelisk.
  6. Teleport to War's Retreat to bank.

c.t: What to do with the pouches
c.g: What to do with the pouches
c.h:
Some options only work well with some pouches, some only work well depending on prices. You should analyse the data and figure out what is the best option for you.

MethodBenefitsDrawbacks
Sell to Grand Exchange.Works for almost every pouch and will generally get a fair price.Sometimes you may be forced to wait for pouches to sell.
Trade to Bogrog or Lord Amlodd for spirit shards. (P2P)Can sometimes save you money over the Grand Exchange; Essentially immediate conversion to coins / shards; many but not all pouches have market value equal to the exchange value at Amlodd after unlocking the 10% exchange boost.Needs a higher level than what is required to make the pouch.
Cast the High Level Alchemy spell on them.Can be a good way to train Magic cheaply.
  • Requires more effort and time that you can spend training Summoning.
  • Many pouches make more cash by selling
  • Many other items are more profitable to alch than any pouch
Use the pouches for skilling or combat.Often this will be a great way to make lots of money off training Summoning.
  • Takes a long time to pay out and will require a lot more capital invested in Summoning.
  • Selling and employing the cash, then buying back when needed, may be more efficient.
Make summoning scrolls from the pouches.You gain a slight bit more experience/charm. In many cases the given scrolls will also be worth slightly more than the pouches.The extra time required to turn pouches into scrolls may not be worth the trivially small extra amount of experience.
Disassemble the pouches.Good source of Powerful Components.Selling the pouches and buying other items may be more efficient.
c.a: What to do with the pouches

c.t: Alternative methods of gaining experience — overview
c.h: Using levelling methods that do not require charms, allows players to save the most valuable ones for later use in higher level familiars.

Players may complete certain activities to receive Summoning experience, including:

  • Familiarisation
  • Penguin Hide and Seek
  • Tears of Guthix
  • Troll Invasion

• Why aren't arctic bears listed?
    • Arctic bears only give slightly more experience per pouch than barker toads, but they cost much more. Also, their secondary ingredient has a very low buy limit so it can be difficult to stock up on.
  • Why aren't any abyssal pouches listed?
    • They are usually difficult to gather but because the Abyss is a great spot for magic and range trainers, it is possible to pick up these charms as they drop two at a time very commonly. However, it is not recommended to make these pouches due to the time spent gathering the charms.
  • Why aren't talon beasts listed?
    • Although the talon beast pouch gives the most experience in game, in order to make talon beast pouches, talon beast charms are needed. The only way to obtain these charms is to play the Temple Trekking activity over and over again to encounter nail beasts that drops them. If players have talon beast charms, then it is recommended that they use them, but talon beast charms usually take more effort to obtain than any other charm. Therefore, it is not recommended to list talon beast pouches as your only option to gain experience.
  • Why does it say to wait so long before using blue charms?
    • Blue charms are harder to obtain and give lots of experience at higher levels. As it is easy to level with the other charms at first, it would be a waste to use your blue charms at early levels when you could gain way more experience in the long run by using them at higher levels.
  • Why should gold charms be saved from levels 28-51?
    • There are not many good gold charm pouches at these levels, and it is better to use green charms and crimson charms for this period.
  • Why should spirit larupias not be made when they are essentially the same as spirit graahks and spirit kyatts?
    • Spirit larupias are in lower demand because they are not quite as useful, so it is better to make the other ones. Also, spirit kyatts can be used in the Piscatoris method of making pouches.
  • Why should ice titans not be made when they are essentially the same as fire titans and moss titans?
    • Ice titans require both an air talisman and a water talisman for every pouch, meaning they take more than twice as long and cost more money.
  • What's the fastest way to make pouches? Where's the closest bank?
    • The fastest way to make pouches is to trade noted ingredients with Pikkupstix in Taverley, buy them back, make pouches and sell them to Pikkupstix, repeating the process until you run out of charms. Despite being the quickest method for creating pouches, with a usage rate of 14,000-16,000 charms per hour at full concentration, it is also a very expensive method and should only be used by players with a considerable amount of coins.
    • When the Voice of Seren is active in the Amlodd Clan area in Prifddinas, you receive 120% (20% extra) experience for making pouches and scrolls at the obelisk there. This obelisk is very close to the Ithell Clan bank, and even closer to the Amlodd teleport of the crystal teleport seed or its attuned variant (which can also be used to teleport directly back to a bank with the Trahaearn or Ithell teleports).
      • The Voice of Seren's buff affects the base XP for the pouch rather than providing bonus XP. This means that the 20% increase from the Voice of Seren will also increase how much bonus experience you get.

This article is about training the Summoning skill, and is required for Summoning training.

There are 5 types of charms used to create every type of Summoning pouch:

  • Gold charm - requires 1 Summoning to use. This is the only charm available in free-to-play
  • Green charm - requires 18 Summoning to use
  • Crimson charm - requires 19 Summoning to use
  • Blue charm - requires 23 Summoning to use
  • Elder charm - requires 81 Summoning to use

There are also 7 types of special charms, used as tertiary ingredients in the creation of certain pouches:

  • Obsidian charm
  • Abyssal charm
  • Talon beast charm
  • Void Knight charms:
    • Ravager charm
    • Shifter charm
    • Spinner charm
    • Torcher charm

c.t: Obtaining charms through general combat and Slayer monsters — overview
c.g: Obtaining charms through general combat and Slayer monsters
c.h:
Common monsters to kill for charms include glacors, rock lobsters, waterfiends, and cockroach soldiers. Most Slayer assignments also have favourable charm drop rates. Monsters vary greatly in the number and type of charms they drop. Players attempting to train Summoning should kill monsters that drop lots of crimson or blue charms, as they offer the best experience-per-charm rates.

See here for a table of monsters which drop charms.

The fastest way to level Summoning is to camp at a monster that drops lots of charms, such as waterfiends or rock lobsters. However, it is also common for players to get charms from training Slayer rather than from camping at a specific monster. It is possible to get enough charms for 99 Summoning by getting 99 Slayer, although it depends on what tasks the player does. If a player is going for 99 in both skills, there is no need for them to camp at a monster specifically for charms. However, if a player does not want to do Slayer or is unable to obtain all the charms that they want purely from Slayer, then there are several monsters that are very good to camp at for charms.

Below are some of the most popular monsters to kill for charm drops.
c.a: Obtaining charms through general combat and Slayer monsters

c.g: Obtaining charms through general combat and Slayer monsters
c.h: Gelatinous abominations have around a 44% charm drop rate. They drop gold charms at about 41%. The gelatinous abominations have only 150 life points and are level 6, so they are really quick and easy kills. The only equipment required is spiked gauntlets, which can be purchased at any Slayer Master. These monsters are found in the Taverley Slayer Dungeon, south-east of Turael (or Spria) in Taverley. Killing these is a great way for anyone to obtain gold charms, but no drops of great value can be obtained, and the combat experience gained is minimal.

c.g: Obtaining charms through general combat and Slayer monsters
c.h:
Suqah have a 35% charm drop rate. They have a charm drop rate of: Gold (14%), Green (8%), Red (6%), Blue (7-8%). While the numbers might seem small, it is very common to get a charm drop about 1/3 kills. The suqah attack with melee, even at a distance, and those on the northern part of the isle attack with melee and a weak version of Ice Barrage or Water Wave on their opponents. However, their damage can add up very fast when they do hit, so food or Guthan's armour is highly recommended.

These are not recommended unless you have at least level 50 in either melee, magic, or ranged. Players must have at least started Lunar Diplomacy to have access to Lunar Isle.

c.g: Obtaining charms through general combat and Slayer monsters
c.h:
Rock crabs have a 13% charm drop rate, 10% of which are gold charms. This can be an efficient way for lower-level players with extra cash to get charms and decent experience. You should also run around and activate all the crabs since they don't attack and won't be able to be attacked unless someone runs next to them. If they stop attacking you, just run south of the crabs, right past the helmet shop and then run back up. This is a great way for lower levels to get charms and ranged experience. You can get around 3-5 charms per minute if you do it correctly.

This is not recommended unless you don't mind spending money to buy cannonballs, since they are very expensive.

c.g: Obtaining charms through general combat and Slayer monsters
c.h:
Moss giants are great for gold charms, about 40% drop rate. They have very low defence and slow attack speed, making them easy to power through even at low levels. North-west of Ardougne has 4 moss giants, and it is, more often than not, empty. Other popular places include the Varrock sewer system and Moss Giant Island. For almost guaranteed seclusion, there are also some moss giants on Crandor. Finally, a decent amount of moss giants can be found in Brimhaven Dungeon (requires 875 coins to enter, or Karamja gloves 3). This area will almost always be empty.

At level 65 Dungeoneering, the Moss Giant Resource Dungeon can be accessed, located at the end of the Varrock Sewers, and is widely regarded as the best place to kill moss giants if you can access the dungeon, with 8 spawns all in close proximity.

c.g: Obtaining charms through general combat and Slayer monsters
c.h: Ice giants are great for gold charms, about 55-57% drop rate for charms. They have relatively low defence and slow attack speed, making them easy to power through even at low levels. Two places to find ice giants are in the ice mountain dungeon and in the Asgarnian Ice Dungeon. They also spawn near the western wilderness wall and the members' fence line.

c.g: Obtaining charms through general combat and Slayer monsters
c.h:
Goblins have an 11% chance to drop a gold charm. The best way to kill goblins is to go to the goblin hut in Lumbridge. It is a bad idea to bring a slow weapon like a godsword, battleaxe, or 2H, as you cannot hit very quickly, resulting in slow progress. A weapon like a whip, scimitar, dagger or claws is ideal so you can do 20-30+ goblins and obtain 2-3 charms per minute. If you camp for an hour, you can easily get 50+ charms. This is not recommended if you cannot frequently hit 50-120 damage.

The goblins across the River Lum near the Al Kharid gate have low life points; keep that in mind when choosing what weapon to use to get one-hit kills (scimitar works best most of the time). The goblins found in the Goblin Village do not drop any charms at all, so it is not advised to go there.

c.g: Obtaining charms through general combat and Slayer monsters
c.h: Abyssal walkers have an 18% green charm rate. They exist in large numbers to the south of the abyss, so you should bring multi-target weapons, such as chinchompas or halberds, and use AoE abilities. This method is recommended for those who have a charming imp set to eat abyssal charms because picking up charms manually would significantly slow down your damage output and the rate of getting charms. The recommended combat stats are the same as for abyss combat training. Using a charming imp, a player with ~75 in attack and strength, while using a halberd, can expect to get 300 green charms per hour. Using charming potions is recommended.

c.g: Obtaining charms through general combat and Slayer monsters
c.h:
Giant rock crabs can be the best monster for acquiring gold charms. They drop three of these at a time quite frequently. The giant rock crabs can be found in the Chaos Tunnels, near the entrance south-west of the Wilderness Crater. It is recommended to use Magic to kill giant rock crabs, since it is their weakness. Bring a few pieces of food, runes for the spell you'll be using, and also some runes for telekinetic grab (if using the standard spellbook). There's a safespot by the stalagmites in the north-east corner of the room.

Another area to kill giant rock crabs is in the Waterbirth Island Dungeon. There are a multitude of them in the northern area beyond the gate. Keep in mind, you will have to run past many Dagannoth in the main part of the first level before entering the rock crab area.

Walk near a boulder, and it will transform into a giant rock crab. Lure it to your safe spot so it gets stuck and you can safely mage it. When near death, the giant rock crab will attempt to flee. Once the crab is dead, it's recommended to use telekinetic grab on the charms so you won't put yourself in danger by going near other crabs.

Ice Burst or Ice Barrage can be used effectively here. Use Protect from Melee or Deflect Melee and gather all the crabs at a spot so that you can burst or barrage them. This method gives the most charms per hour.

A disadvantage of killing giant rock crabs is that the charms gained are mostly gold, which is the lowest-level charm. Comparatively, the charms that can be gained in a given time period from killing giant rock crabs will not give as much summoning experience as the charms that can be gained in the same time period from killing a monster that drops mainly higher-level charms, such as waterfiends or rock lobsters. Giant rock crabs should only be killed at low-level summoning when gold charms are most useful, and even then, it is important to realise that since charms can be saved up, it probably would be more worth your time to just start at a monster that drops primarily crimson charms right away, since you will end up getting gold charms to make it through the low summoning levels anyway, at the same time as you save up tons of crimsons to use later.

c.g: Obtaining charms through general combat and Slayer monsters
c.h: With the introduction of infernal ashes, killing black demons became another reasonable method of gathering crimson charms. The ashes cover the cost of the cannonballs and other consumables. At higher levels, such as with 70 Agility, 52/68/96 Summoning, a chaotic weapon, and 80+ combat stats, a player can amass profit above 200k per hour on top of the crimson charms. High ranged levels help too, as demons are weak to bolts.

c.g: Obtaining charms through general combat and Slayer monsters
c.h:
Killing rock lobsters is often considered to be the fastest way to train Summoning, although waterfiends can actually be faster than bursting with the optimal levels and equipment, including 99 Summoning for a Steel titan. Rock lobsters do not require a high Summoning level to kill quickly.

The best way to kill rock lobsters is to use Ice Barrage or Ice Burst since they are aggressive. There are many different ways to do this successfully, most of which involve luring 9 rock lobsters towards you while using Protect from Melee or Deflect Melee, moving to a safe spot, then casting the spells to kill them. Armour that gives high magic and/or prayer bonuses is recommended. Most of your inventory should be Prayer potions, but you will also want runes for ice spells and a few blood spells (to heal, as you can take damage from Dagannoths using a ranged attack). Also, bring a teleport and a few pieces of food.

Due to an update, you can now reach rock lobsters without a partner.

Players attempting to use this method to kill rock lobsters should have 70+ (preferably 94+) Magic and 70+ Prayer. They should also have a lot of cash, as this method is costly due to the runes and prayer potions used.

Ice-bursting rock lobsters can give over 180 crimson charms per hour, whereas ice barraging can give up to 270 crimson charms per hour.

To further improve the number of crimson charms players get and how many runes they use, many players choose to use damage-increasing variables such as the staff of light, arcane stream necklace, arcane blast necklace, or arcane pulse necklace as well as the wolpertinger special move, Magic Focus, which boosts Magic level.

c.g: Obtaining charms through general combat and Slayer monsters
c.h:
Waterfiends are a great source of crimson charms for mid-to-high level players. They are weak to bolts and easy to kill with a royal crossbow or another tier 75+ ranged weapon. Waterfiends can be killed in the Ancient Cavern or in the Chaos Tunnels. Waterfiends have a ranged attack and a magic attack. The magic attack is more dangerous.

Mid-level players will find it easiest to kill Waterfiends in the Ancient Caverns. Using a royal crossbow and a healing familiar such as a bunyip, it is easy to obtain about 150 crimson charms per hour.

Higher-level players, with 95+ Ranged and Defence, will find that little healing is necessary. Such players may want to bring a combat familiar instead of a healing familiar. Using extreme potions and turmoil, high-level players can obtain about 225 crimson charms per hour in the Ancient Cavern.

For an even higher rate of charm collecting, very high-level players can choose to kill Waterfiends in the Chaos Tunnels, where they are denser. Here, players should use Soul Split, an Iron or Steel titan loaded with the appropriate scrolls, extreme potions, and the highest level crossbow and ranged armour possible. If making full use of multi-target abilities, players can expect to earn about 300 charms per hour in the chaos tunnels.

c.g: Obtaining charms through general combat and Slayer monsters
c.h: For higher-level players with 81+ Slayer, killing gladii at the Monastery of Ascension allows for a fast way to collect crimson charms while also serving as a money making method. Like other Order of Ascension members, gladii are weak against ranged weapons and have a weakness to any ranged attack type, and they are almost impossible to kill at any decent speed with magic or melee. At high range levels and using extreme ranging potions and a level 80+ weapon, over 150 crimson charms per hour can be obtained, making them only slightly inferior to waterfiends and rock lobsters for training. Unlike these monsters, gladii can also yield a significant profit of 2m+ per hour as a result of their valuable ascension keystone drops, as well as their frequent drops of noted resources and rune and adamant alchables, making them one of only a few ways to profitably and quickly train Summoning. To kill gladii, it is recommended to rely on some healing method other than food to lengthen trip duration, such as the bunyip or unicorn stallion familiars, or the Soul Split curse. Gladii are relatively safe to kill, as they do not inflict much damage, but they can inflict stuns and binds using their special attack, so usage of the Anticipation and Freedom abilities is recommended to not lose killing efficiency. Royal d'hide, Armadyl or Pernix armours should be worn to maximise kill speeds, and a ring of Wealth to increase profits.

c.g: Obtaining charms through general combat and Slayer monsters
c.h: Bork can be killed for repetitive guaranteed charm drops. The minimum he will drop on death is 5 crimson or 2 green charms. The Familiarisation D&D will not triple these charm drops.

c.g: Obtaining charms through general combat and Slayer monsters
c.h:
Tormented demons are excellent monsters for obtaining blue charms. On average, around 3 charms per 2 kills will be obtained. A strategy guide is available at here.

Glacors are also excellent monsters for obtaining blue and crimson charms. They drop 3 per kill and have roughly the same per cent chance of dropping blue or crimson. A strategy guide is available at here.

c.g: Obtaining charms through general combat and Slayer monsters
c.h:
Using a dwarf multicannon on the 10 greater demons in the Forinthry Dungeon can net 200+ crimson charms an hour. It is recommended to bring Prayer urns to collect the massive amount of Accursed Ashes that will be dropped, which will give prayer experience as well as greatly clean up the drops on the ground. The Forinthry Dungeon is in the Wilderness; the greater demons within are located in levels 20-24, so if using this method, it is recommended to have a teleport item handy (such as an amulet of glory), and do not bring anything you are not willing to lose.

Dying in the Wilderness will cause you to drop all of your items if you are skulled.

c.g: Obtaining charms through general combat and Slayer monsters
c.h: Hellhounds, while not advised for green, crimson, or blue charms, have a 68-69% drop rate for gold charms and can be safely spotted in most of their locations. If you have high enough ranged or magic skills to swiftly kill them, you can quickly collect gold charms in safety. Another great method is to use a Guthan's set, a bonecrusher and a bone necklace in combination with the Piety prayer. Unfortunately, hellhounds have very poor drops and aren't profitable (not counting the rewards of any possible clue scrolls you may find). An alternative for gold charms is fire giants with around a 55% drop rate for gold charms, and they are much easier to kill with additional good loot.

c.g: Obtaining charms through general combat and Slayer monsters
c.h:
Cave bugs have a 40% green charm drop rate, the second highest in-game after mithril dragons. They are level 11 and fairly easy to kill. Only the level 11 ones drop charms; level 6 cave bugs drop no charms at all.

With dragon or better armour and an abyssal whip, one can easily achieve 40+ green charms an hour at levels 70 attack and 70 strength. One place to kill them is the Dorgesh-Kaan South Dungeon, where there's a convenient fishing spot where you can fish for frogspawns and a fairy ring nearby. Another is in the Chaos Tunnels.

c.g: Obtaining charms through general combat and Slayer monsters
c.h:
With high melee stats (preferably 90+, Turmoil, Soul Split, and unicorn stallion), it is possible to obtain over 115 crimson charms an hour from the King Black Dragon, while making about 350-500k an hour profit. This can be a rather attractive way to obtain charms for high-level players, as the charm-obtaining rate is very good while making a profit rather than losing a lot from bursting rock lobsters.

However, this method requires the ability to make super antifire potions, so that players can use an off-hand weapon or 2h weapon rather than a dragonfire shield in order to increase its efficiency.

c.t: Kalphite Queen or Exiled Kalphite Queen
c.g: Obtaining charms through general combat and Slayer monsters
c.h:
With high combat stats, it is possible to obtain a decent amount of charms per hour from the Kalphite Queen/Exiled Kalphite Queen, while making a profit of 600-800k per hour. This is helpful as the queen drops various charms, with the exiled version dropping much more than the regular variant. The regular Queen drops 6 charms, while the exiled one drops 9.

However, the queen is very tough and has several guards, so players may need to rebank much more often.
c.a: Kalphite Queen or Exiled Kalphite Queen

c.g: Obtaining charms through general combat and Slayer monsters
c.h: Exiled kalphite guardians drop blue charms at a very high rate. This makes it incredibly fast and easy to obtain blues without completing high-level quests for tormented demons or glacors. However, the Exiled Kalphite Marauders provide a slightly better rate for blue charms and can be killed while AFK at higher levels.

c.g: Obtaining charms through general combat and Slayer monsters
c.h:
Exiled kalphite guardians and Exiled kalphite marauders have a very high blue and crimson charm drop rate, low health, fast spawn rate, high concentration, and can be killed while AFK.

This method can yield 550+ blue charms, 500+ crimson charms, and 350+ green charms per hour while near full AFK (just keeping prayer/potions up). Additionally, the Charm drop enhancer can be used to double (base + 1 from charming potion +2 from drop enhancer) this rate for 40 minutes once per week (or twice if using Distraction & Diversion reset token (weekly)).

This method has no strict requirements, but each piece of the setup increases the rate at which charms are collected, makes AFK easier, or reduces the running cost.

Worn equipment information

  • Dragon Rider helm reduces prayer drain.
  • Ancient Book reduces prayer drain (any God book will work).
  • Dragon Rider cape reduces prayer drain.
  • Dragon Rider amulet reduces prayer drain.
  • Tirannwn quiver 4 reduces prayer drain.
  • Superior Dragon Rider boots reduces prayer drain.
  • Cinderbane gloves increase kills per hour by doing poison damage.
  • Augmented noxious staff should ideally have Caroming 4 Equilibrium 2 + Precise 6 Ruthless 1.
  • Augmented Virtus robe top and Augmented Virtus robe legs should ideally have some combination of Scavenging 4 Crackling 4 Biting 4 and any other perk in the 4th slot.
  • Asylum surgeon's ring increases kills per hour slightly.

Inventory information

  • Holy overload potion (6) increases kills per hour and restores prayer points.
  • Charming potion (4) adds 1 extra charm per drop.
  • Weapon poison+++ (4) increases kills per hour (five doses are worth an hour).
  • Super restore (4) restores prayer points (often cheaper than Prayer potion (4)).
  • Steel titan pouch and Steel Titan scroll (Steel of Legends) increases kills per hour.
  • Oldak coil increases kills per hour.
  • Spring cleaner 9001 converts salvage into coin automatically (converted salvage pays for the spring cost).
  • Herb bag stores auto-picked-up grimy herbs.
  • Spirit gem bag stores auto-picked-up spirit gems.

Additional recommended items

  • Penance reduces the prayer upkeep.
  • Advanced gold accumulator auto picks up coin drops.
  • Seedicide with the auto-pickup upgrade configured to pick up herb seeds to sell/use.
  • Herbicide with the auto-pickup upgrade configured to pick up all grimy herbs to sell/use. Picked up herbs go directly into the Herb bag.
  • Charming imp auto-picks up charms and spirit gems.
  • Oldak coil upgrade kit increases the damage the oldak coil does.
  • Restocking cannon perk to auto restock the oldak coil.
  • Soul Split to heal during combat.
  • Torment to increase damage and kills per hour.
  • Air Surge the strongest air spell in the standard magic book.
  • A Revolution++ bar that favors AOE abilities.

With the listed items (or the best match if not everything is available), head to the Exiled Kalphite Hive and set up the Oldak coil directly east of the stalagmites at the end of the hive with one tile between the coil and the stalagmites. Next, stand on the west side of the stalagmites, leaving one tile between you and the stalagmites. Enable auto-retaliate, summon the Steel Titan, give it the special scrolls, activate Soul Split, Torment, drink 1 dose of Holy overload potion, Weapon poison+++, and Charming potion. After this, just keep restoring prayer and re-up potions as they expire.

The herbs and seeds collected will more than cover the running cost of all materials used. The cannon increases the kill rate enough that the additional herbs dropped more than pay for the cannonballs used.
cn: Spring cleaner 9001 converts salvage into coin automatically (converted salvage pays for the spring cost)

c.g: Obtaining charms through general combat and Slayer monsters
c.h: The Troll brute and Troll chucker are the only two monsters that drop charms on non-members worlds. They only drop Gold charms on these worlds, and rarely drop green, crimson and blue charms on members' worlds. They are only level 2 monsters, which makes them ideal for lower-level players. Average and high-level members have much better ways to get charms.

c.g: Obtaining charms through general combat and Slayer monsters
c.h:
The Slayer creatures in the Monastery of Ascension come in four varieties. Each one dominates a single charm type, with another charm as an uncommon drop.

  • Rorarius - mainly drops gold charms.
  • Capsarius - mainly drops green charms.
  • Gladius - mainly drops crimson charms.
  • Scutarius - mainly drops crimson and blue charms.
  • Legiones - mainly drops crimson and blue charms.

• Looting Dorgesh-Kaan Average Chest (requires level 52 Thieving).
  • Looting Dorgesh-Kaan Rich Chest (requires level 78 Thieving).
  • Pickpocketing Amlodd workers in Prifddinas (requires 94 Thieving and the completion of the Plague's End quest). All four charms are common loot.
  • Pickpocketing Menaphite marketeers (requires 46 Thieving) and opening small Menaphite gifts. Using the Sticky Fingers relic power is recommended.
  • Looting Zanaris Market trinket stall (requires 116 thieving).

• Spirit impling (requires level 54 Hunter)
    • Spirit implings are difficult to find and primarily give tertiary summoning items, though do also sometimes give charms.
  • Charm sprite (requires level 72 Hunter)
    • Charm sprites are notable for having a high output ratio of blue charms to the total number of other charms, and provide a good alternative to skillers.
  • Charming moths (requires level 88 Hunter and level 83 Agility)
    • Charming moths have high gold and green charm outputs and are slightly faster than charm sprites (340 charms per hour versus roughly 300 charms) with a chance to get crystal triskelion fragments, but they require higher levels and are located in the Wilderness.

When adding logs to a bonfire, fire spirits sometimes arise from the flames. A common reward for freeing them is charms of all four types. Free players cannot obtain any charms, not even Gold, from bonfires.

The chance of a fire spirit appearing is quintupled when using either a crystal tinderbox or an augmented crystal tinderbox. When burning maple logs, this allows the player to gain an average of 44 gold charms, 144 green charms, 18 crimson charms, and 9 blue charms per hour.
Charms may be obtained through the Soul Wars reward shop.

Once per week, the Familiarisation Distraction and Diversion can be done, which gives a reward of 40 minutes of triple charm drops. It is recommended to use this time by killing a monster that drops a lot of crimson charms.
The tetracompasses from the Archaeology skill can sometimes give 50 blue charms as part of the reward for completing one.

If you have 21 Summoning and spent some time training Dungeoneering, you can buy a charming imp, which automatically picks up requested charms and converts unwanted charms into small Summoning experience. This can increase the rate of gathering charms significantly and it increases the amount of Combat or Slayer experience earned (per hour). It is highly encouraged to configure the imp to give the player all types of charms; the experience rewarded for converting the charms is much lower than the amount offered by using the charms to make pouches.
The Fang of Mohegan may also be used to provide a slight possibility of a double charm drop.

The charming potion is a potion that increases the base number of charms dropped by a monster by 1 for 6 minutes. Special charms such as abyssal charms and talon beast charms are affected by the potion.
